subject: NEET PG Strategy
title: Weightage & Subject Sequencing Strategy
preview: Plan subject sequencing around deficits and exam utility rather than an unverifiable fixed weightage percentage.

sections.title: Prioritize what matters
points: Group mistakes by genuine knowledge gap, interpretation error and exam pacing problem.
Spend more time on weaknesses with high clinical or examination relevance while maintaining broad coverage.

sections.title: Measure progress
points: Review the trend in accuracy and speed on unseen questions rather than only familiar flashcards.
Use shorter frequent reviews of forgotten material across the revision period.

sections.title: Exam trap
points: No single fixed subject-weightage percentage applies reliably to every future examination.
More study hours are not useful if they do not improve retention or transfer to questions.

quickRevision: Identify personal weak topics using recent mock results and missed-question patterns.
Allocate time based on the importance of each topic, learning gap and days available.
Use spaced active recall and mixed-case practice rather than only rereading notes.

quiz.question: What best determines revision sequencing?
options: Weakness, importance and available study time
quiz.explanation: A useful revision sequence weighs weak subjects, expected examination relevance and available time rather than following a fixed subject-order formula.
